question: What name did Anne Frank affectionately give to her diary? 📓
explanation: Excellent! Anne felt she didn't have a true friend to confide in, so she treated her diary as her best friend and named it 'Kitty'. 🖋️
hint: It sounds like a common name for a pet cat.

question: According to Anne, what has more patience than people? ⏳
explanation: Spot on! Anne believed that 'paper has more patience than people' because it listens silently without judging or interrupting. 📝
hint: It is something you write on.

question: How old was Anne when she started writing her diary? 🎂
explanation: Awesome! Anne received the diary as a gift for her thirteenth birthday and started recording her life shortly after. 🎉
hint: She had just officially become a teenager.

question: What was the name of Anne's older sister? 👧
explanation: Great job! Margot was Anne's older sister, who was three years older than her. 👭
hint: Her name starts with the letter 'M'.

question: What subject did Mr. Keesing teach Anne's class? 📚
explanation: Correct! Mr. Keesing was the strict old fogey who taught Maths at Anne's school. 🔢
hint: This subject involves numbers, geometry, and algebra.

question: Why was Mr. Keesing constantly annoyed with Anne? 😠
options: She talked too much in class 🗣️
answer: She talked too much in class 🗣️
explanation: Fantastic! Mr. Keesing was annoyed because Anne was very talkative and wouldn't stay quiet during his lessons. 🤐
hint: She used her mouth a bit too much during class time.

question: What was the topic of the first essay Mr. Keesing assigned to Anne as a punishment? ✍️
explanation: Brilliant! The very first punishment essay she had to write was simply titled 'A Chatterbox'. 📝
hint: It is a single noun describing someone who talks a lot.

question: How did Anne justify her talkative nature in her first essay? 🧠
options: She said it was a student's trait and inherited 🧬
She blamed it on her friends 👯
She said the class was boring 😴
answer: She said it was a student's trait and inherited 🧬
explanation: Spot on! She humorously argued that talking is a student's trait and that she inherited the habit from her mother, so she couldn't do much about it. 👩‍👧
hint: She claimed she got it from her mother.

question: What was the title of the second essay Mr. Keesing assigned to Anne? 📄
explanation: Awesome! When she didn't stop talking, he assigned a second essay titled 'An Incorrigible Chatterbox', meaning a habit that cannot be corrected. 📚
hint: It contains a big word meaning 'not able to be corrected'.

question: Who helped Anne write her third assignment in verse? ✍️
explanation: Excellent! Her friend Sanne, who was good at poetry, offered to help Anne write the essay from beginning to end in verse. 📜
hint: It was a friend whose name rhymes with 'Anne'.

question: In Anne's poetic essay, what did the Father Swan do to his three ducklings? 🦢
explanation: Great job! In her dark humored poem, the Father Swan bit the ducklings to death because they quacked too much. 🦢
hint: He did something very harsh because they made too much noise.

question: How did Mr. Keesing react to Anne's poem about the ducklings? 😂
options: He took the joke the right way and laughed 🤣
He assigned her ten more essays 📚
answer: He took the joke the right way and laughed 🤣
explanation: Spot on! Mr. Keesing understood the humor, read the poem to the class, and finally allowed Anne to talk without giving her extra homework. 🎓
hint: He found it funny instead of getting angry.

question: Why did Anne feel lonely even though she had loving parents and friends? 😔
options: She didn't have a true, intimate friend to confide in 🤝
answer: She didn't have a true, intimate friend to confide in 🤝
explanation: Awesome! Anne had people around her, but she couldn't bring herself to talk about anything but ordinary everyday things. She lacked a deep connection. 🫂
hint: She had friends for fun, but no one to share deep secrets with.

question: What does an autobiography mean in literary terms? 📖
options: A life story written by the person themselves ✍️
answer: A life story written by the person themselves ✍️
explanation: Brilliant! An autobiography is when an author writes the story of their own life, just like Anne writing about her own experiences in her diary. 📓
hint: The prefix 'auto-' means self.

question: Who was Mrs. Kuperus in Anne's life? 🏫
explanation: Excellent! Mrs. Kuperus was the headmistress at Anne's Montessori nursery school. They had a very emotional farewell. 😢
hint: She was a teacher figure from Anne's early childhood.

question: Why was Anne's entire class 'quaking in its boots'? 👢
options: Teachers were deciding who would move up to the next form 📈
A scary dog entered the room 🐕
answer: Teachers were deciding who would move up to the next form 📈
explanation: Spot on! The students were nervous because the teachers' meeting would decide who passes and who stays back in the same class. 😰
hint: They were worried about their academic results.

question: According to Anne, what are the 'most unpredictable creatures on earth'? 👽
explanation: Awesome! Anne humorously calls teachers the most unpredictable creatures because students never know how they will grade or decide their fate. 🎲
hint: They are the ones who grade the exam papers.

question: When Anne writes 'paper has more patience than people', what is she seeking? 🔍
options: A quiet escape to express her true feelings 💭
answer: A quiet escape to express her true feelings 💭
explanation: Great job! She uses the diary as an outlet for her internal conflict and loneliness because paper won't interrupt or judge her. 📝
hint: She wants a safe space to share her deepest thoughts.

question: What did Anne do to show she still loved and missed her grandmother? 🕯️
options: She lit a candle for her on her own birthday 🎂
answer: She lit a candle for her on her own birthday 🎂
explanation: Brilliant! During Anne's birthday celebration in 1942, Grandma's candle was lit along with the rest to honor her memory. 🕯️
hint: She did something special with fire on her birthday.

question: What does the phrase 'plunge right in' mean when Anne starts writing her diary entries? 🏊‍♀️
options: To start writing directly without an introduction ✍️
To throw the diary in water 💧
answer: To start writing directly without an introduction ✍️
explanation: Spot on! Though she wanted to 'plunge right in', she decided to provide a brief sketch of her life first so people could understand her entries. 📖
hint: It means to begin something immediately.

question: Switching to the poem 'Amanda!', who is most likely speaking to Amanda in the poem? 🗣️
explanation: Excellent! The tone is authoritative and nagging, suggesting it is a parent or a guardian constantly instructing Amanda. 🏡
hint: This person tells her to clean her room and sit up straight.

question: What is Amanda doing that prompts the speaker to say 'Stop that slouching'? 🛋️
explanation: Awesome! 'Slouching' means sitting or standing in a lazy, drooping way, and her parent wants her to sit up straight. 📏
hint: It means not maintaining a straight posture.

question: How does Amanda escape the nagging instructions in the poem? 🌈
options: By drifting into her own imagination 💭
answer: By drifting into her own imagination 💭
explanation: Great job! Amanda practices 'escapism'. Whenever she is scolded, she mentally transports herself to fantasy worlds to find peace. 🧚‍♀️
hint: She travels to other worlds inside her mind.

question: In her first daydream, what creature does Amanda imagine herself to be? 🧜‍♀️
explanation: Brilliant! She imagines herself as the sole inhabitant of a beautiful, languid emerald sea, drifting blissfully as a mermaid. 🌊
hint: A mythical creature with a fish tail.

question: Why does Amanda imagine herself as an orphan? 👤
options: She wants to roam the streets freely without anyone nagging her 🚶‍♀️
She wants to ask for money 🪙
She wants to live in an orphanage 🏠
answer: She wants to roam the streets freely without anyone nagging her 🚶‍♀️
explanation: Spot on! Being an orphan in her daydream symbolizes ultimate freedom. She just wants to walk barefoot in the dust without rules. 👣
hint: She craves independence and no parental supervision.

question: What does Amanda make with her bare feet in her daydream? 👣
explanation: Awesome! She imagines roaming the street and quietly making patterns in the soft dust with her bare, hushed feet. 🏜️
hint: She draws shapes on the dusty ground.

question: In the poem, how does Amanda describe 'silence' and 'freedom'? 🤫
options: Silence is golden, freedom is sweet 🍯
Silence is boring, freedom is scary 😱
Silence is heavy, freedom is light 🪶
Silence is silver, freedom is gold 🏅
answer: Silence is golden, freedom is sweet 🍯
explanation: Excellent! She values peace so much that she says 'The silence is golden, the freedom is sweet' while daydreaming. 🌟
hint: Golden and sweet.

question: What is Amanda forbidden to eat because it might cause acne? 🍫
explanation: Great job! Her parent says, 'Don't eat that chocolate, Amanda! Remember your acne, Amanda!' 🍫
hint: It is a sweet, brown treat made from cocoa.

question: Which fairy tale character does Amanda imagine herself to be in a tower? 🏰
explanation: Brilliant! She wants to be Rapunzel living in a high tower where life is 'tranquil and rare' (peaceful and unique). 🏰
hint: She is a princess known for her very long hair.

question: What is the key difference between Amanda and the real Rapunzel? 💇‍♀️
options: Amanda will never let down her bright hair 👱‍♀️
answer: Amanda will never let down her bright hair 👱‍♀️
explanation: Spot on! Unlike Rapunzel, who let down her hair for a prince, Amanda wants to stay completely alone and undisturbed forever. 🤫
hint: She doesn't want anyone to climb up to her.

question: What is the speaker's main concern at the very end of the poem 'Amanda!'? 🤔
options: That Amanda will fail her exams 📚
That people will think the speaker nagged Amanda 🗣️
answer: That people will think the speaker nagged Amanda 🗣️
explanation: Awesome! The parent says, 'Anyone would think that I nagged at you, Amanda!' showing they care more about society's opinion than Amanda's feelings. 👥
hint: They are worried about their own reputation.

question: Why are the stanzas describing Amanda's imagination placed in brackets ( )? 📝
options: To show they are her internal, silent thoughts 💭
Because they are spoken by the parent 🗣️
answer: To show they are her internal, silent thoughts 💭
explanation: Excellent! The brackets visually separate the harsh reality (the parent's nagging) from Amanda's peaceful internal daydreaming. 🧠
hint: It indicates a shift into someone's mind.

question: What does the repeated use of the name 'Amanda!' at the end of each instruction highlight? 📢
options: The musical rhythm of the name 🎵
The strict, authoritative, and nagging tone of the speaker 🗣️
answer: The strict, authoritative, and nagging tone of the speaker 🗣️
explanation: Great job! Constantly repeating her name with an exclamation mark shows how demanding and overbearing the parent is being. 😠
hint: It makes it sound like she is constantly in trouble.

question: What literary device is used in the phrase 'Stop that slouching and sit up straight'? 🔤
explanation: Brilliant! The repetition of the 's' sound in 'Stop', 'slouching', 'sit', and 'straight' is a perfect example of alliteration. 🎶
hint: It's the repetition of the same starting consonant sound.

question: How does Amanda react to the continuous scolding? 😶
options: She withdraws into her own fantasy world 🧚‍♀️
answer: She withdraws into her own fantasy world 🧚‍♀️
explanation: Spot on! Instead of fighting back, she uses 'escapism', retreating into her beautiful, peaceful imagination. 🌌
hint: She ignores reality and starts dreaming.

question: What does the word 'languid' mean when Amanda describes the emerald sea? 🌊
explanation: Awesome! 'Languid' means slow and relaxed. Amanda wants a peaceful environment, entirely opposite to her chaotic real life. 🏝️
hint: It means the opposite of rushed or stressed.

question: Why does the speaker call Amanda 'moody'? 😒
options: Because she doesn't respond to the scolding and looks sulky 😶
Because she changes her clothes often 👗
answer: Because she doesn't respond to the scolding and looks sulky 😶
explanation: Excellent! Since Amanda is daydreaming and not paying attention, her face looks unresponsive and upset, which the parent labels as 'moody'. 😕
hint: She looks like she is in a bad mood.

question: What common theme connects both Anne Frank's diary and the poem 'Amanda!'? 🔗
options: Both were hiding from a war 🛡️
Both highlight the internal conflict and feelings of misunderstood youth 🧠
answer: Both highlight the internal conflict and feelings of misunderstood youth 🧠
explanation: Great job! Both texts beautifully capture the minds of teenagers who feel misunderstood by the adults around them and seek an outlet (a diary or daydreams). 🤝
hint: It is about how teenagers feel around adults.

question: Who is the poet of the poem 'Amanda!'? ✒️
explanation: Brilliant! The poem 'Amanda!' was written by Australian author Robin Klein, known for her books for children and young adults. 📚
hint: The first name is the name of a bird with a red breast.

question: In her diary, Anne writes about her father, Otto Frank. How does she describe him? 👨
options: The most adorable father she had ever seen ❤️
answer: The most adorable father she had ever seen ❤️
explanation: Spot on! Anne had a deep affection for her father and described him as the most adorable father she had ever met. 🥰
hint: She had very positive and loving feelings towards him.

question: Before going into hiding, in which city did Anne's family live in the Netherlands? 🏙️
explanation: Awesome! Anne's family emigrated to Holland and lived in Amsterdam before they had to go into hiding. 🇳🇱
hint: It is the capital city of the Netherlands.

question: What was the name of the boy Anne refers to while talking about her classmates in the diary? 👦
explanation: Excellent! When talking about who will pass the class, she mentions her friend G.N. and herself laughing at two boys, C.N. and Jacques. 😂
hint: A French-sounding name.

question: In 'Amanda!', what chore is Amanda asked if she has finished? 🧹
explanation: Great job! The speaker asks, 'Did you tidy your room, Amanda?' along with checking if she cleaned her shoes. 👟
hint: Making sure the place she sleeps is clean.

question: What is Anne Frank's diary originally written in? 📝
explanation: Brilliant! Although her family was German, she grew up in the Netherlands and wrote her famous diary in the Dutch language. 📖
hint: The language spoken in the Netherlands.

question: What literary concept is shown when Amanda creates a 'persona' of a mermaid or Rapunzel? 🎭
explanation: Spot on! Escapism is the tendency to seek distraction and relief from unpleasant realities, especially by seeking entertainment or engaging in fantasy. 🌌
hint: Running away from reality into the imagination.

question: Why did Anne want to keep a diary in the first place? 🤔
options: To submit it for a school project 🎒
To get all kinds of things off her chest 🗣️
answer: To get all kinds of things off her chest 🗣️
explanation: Awesome! She says she has an even greater need to write to get all kinds of things off her chest since she has no real friend. 🤍
hint: To express her hidden, buried feelings.

question: What does the speaker in 'Amanda!' tell her NOT to do with her shoulders? 🤷‍♀️
explanation: Excellent! The poem starts with 'Don't hunch your shoulders, Amanda!' as a correction to her bad posture. 📏
hint: It means to bend them forward lazily.

question: In Mr. Keesing's class, what made Anne finally laugh during the second essay assignment? 😂
options: A funny joke by a friend 👯
The fact she had exhausted nearly all her ideas on chatterboxes 🤯
A bird flying into the room 🐦
answer: The fact she had exhausted nearly all her ideas on chatterboxes 🤯
explanation: Great job! By the time she got the third assignment ('Quack, Quack, Quack'), she had exhausted her ingenuity on the topic of chatterboxes and had to laugh. 🤣
hint: She ran out of original ideas on the topic.

question: What does Amanda's desire for 'golden silence' tell us about her environment? 🔊
options: It is filled with constant, noisy nagging 🗣️
answer: It is filled with constant, noisy nagging 🗣️
explanation: Brilliant! Because she is constantly being scolded and instructed, her environment is noisy and stressful. Thus, silence feels 'golden' and precious to her. 🏆
hint: Think about why someone would crave silence so much.

question: According to Anne Frank, what do people usually lack when reading someone else's diary? 📖
explanation: Spot on! This relates back to her famous quote: 'Paper has more patience than people.' People often lack the patience to truly listen or understand. ❤️
hint: It is the quality that paper has more of.
